answer: Require uncorrelated-verifier quorums: a new identity earns rights only after its work is checked by reviewers from at least three unrelated network neighborhoods, never its own introducers. A haven of sock puppets cannot self-certify, since approval must cross clusters sharing no funding, hardware, or history. Like a raven sighted by watchers before it counts, each endorsement is weighted by reviewer distance from the applicant. A tide of fakes stalls at the gate: forging diversity means infiltrating many independent groups at once, far costlier than spawning identities.
